text.p: Yahoo! Inc on Wednesday reported better-than-expected first quarter financial results and said its traffic surged to an average of more than 30 million page views a day in March.
This was up 50 percent from the 20 million page views a day Yahoo reported in December.
Yahoo reported net income of $210,000, or 1 cent a share in the first quarter, up from net income of $81,000 in the year ago first quarter.

Revenues soared to $9.5 million, more than $1 milllion above Wall Street estimates and up from $1.7 million in the first quarter of 1996. Yahoo went public a year ago amid a flurry of Internet stock offerings.
The 1 cent-per-share profit beat Wall Street expectations of a 3 cents-per-share loss for the leading Internet search and media company.
"It's a company that's hitting on all cylinders," said Paul Noglows, Internet analyst at Hambrecht & Quist.

Tim Koogle, Yahoo's chief executive officer, said the company was pleased by the five-fold increase in Internet traffic, as measured by each electronic page displayed in response to a user request, compared with a year ago.
But he also said the growing Internet media company will continue to focus on growing its businesses and developing a brand that is recognised on a wordwide basis.
Yahoo! said it had added several major advertising accounts during the quarter, including Johnson & Johnson, Lufthansa, Novell Inc. and United Parcel Service.
